extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners preparing or prosecuting reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, formal, and substantive requirements and examiner guidance for preparing, filing, and examining patent reissue applications (including ownership submissions, specification/drawings format, new matter, original-patent requirement, overlooked aspects, and recapture analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee consent/signature authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: The consent of an assignee must be signed by a party authorized to act on behalf of the assignee. An appropriate paper satisfying the requirements of 37 CFR 3.73 must be submitted in reply to this Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must verify the signer is authorized to act for the assignee (see MPEP § 1410.01). Use form paragraphs as directed when consent/signature authority issues are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to sign must be stated or shown
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who signed the submission establishing ownership interest must state in what capacity the submission on behalf of the corporation or other business entity was signed; otherwise the signer must be established as authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the submission establishing ownership may be signed by a patent practitioner of record (see 37 CFR 3.73; MPEP § 325). Use form paragraph 14.16.02 when the capacity is not stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of recognized capacity results in objection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person who signed the submission is not recognized as an officer of the assignee and has not been established as authorized to act on behalf of the assignee, the submission is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.16.03; see MPEP § 324 (for applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012) and § 325 (for applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney/agent signature for pre-2012 reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For reissue applications filed before Sept. 16, 2012, an attorney or agent of record is not authorized to sign a submission establishing ownership interest unless established as authorized to act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 14.16.04.fti for these situations. In bracket 1 insert either 'attorney' or 'agent'. For reissue applications filed on or after Sept. 16, 2012, the submission may be signed by a patent practitioner of record per 37 CFR 3.73(d)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance when signed by non-recognized officer requires empowerment statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person other than a recognized officer may sign a submission establishing ownership interest provided the record includes a duly signed statement that the person is empowered to sign the submission and/or act on behalf of the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separately filed paper referencing the previously filed submission and containing a proper empowerment statement is acceptable. Inclusion of the person's title is desirable but not mandatory. This form paragraph MUST be preceded by form paragraphs 14.16.02, 14.16.03, or 14.16.04.fti (see 14.16.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing ownership of patent may suffice for reissue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the submission establishes the assignee’s ownership as to the patent, the assignee’s ownership as to the reissue application will be presumed; a submission as to the ownership of the patent will be construed to satisfy 37 CFR 1.172 (and 37 CFR 3.73) requirements for establishing ownership of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if a submission under 37 CFR 3.73 is present in the patent file but not in the reissue application file, a copy of that submission for the patent must be submitted in the reissue file. Documentation establishing ownership of the reissue application must include the chain of title as to the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must compare assignee on consent and documentary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must inspect both the consent and documentary evidence of ownership to determine whether the requirements of 37 CFR 1.172 have been met; the documentary evidence must identify the same assignee that signed the consent and the persons signing must have authority to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 324 and 325 for further guidance; ensure signers' authority is established on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue application must contain entire printed patent specification and claims (formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.173(a)(1) the application specification, including the claims, of the patent for which reissue is requested must be furnished in the form of a copy of the printed patent, in double column format, each page on only one side of a single sheet of paper. No new matter shall be introduced into the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each page of the patent must appear on only one side of each individual page of the specification of the reissue application; a two-sided copy is not proper. If changes are so extensive that reading is extremely difficult and error-prone, a clean copy of the specification may be submitted if accompanied by a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 for waiver of 37 CFR 1.125(d) and 1.173(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: clean copies and change rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must submit a clean copy of each drawing sheet of the printed patent at the time the reissue application is filed. If such copy complies with 37 CFR 1.84, no further drawings will be required; where drawings include changes, the changes must be made in accordance with 37 CFR 1.173(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not transfer drawings from the patent file to the reissue application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments at time of filing: methods and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments may be made at filing either by (A) physically incorporating changes within the specification by cutting the column of the printed patent and inserting added material and rejoining (markings per 37 CFR 1.173(d) must be used), preserving columnar structure and complying with 37 CFR 1.52(a)(1); or (B) providing a preliminary amendment (a separate amendment paper) directing specified changes be made to the copy of the printed patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As to 1.52(a)(1)(iv), the 'written either by a typewriter or machine printer in permanent dark ink or its equivalent' requirement is deemed satisfied where a caret and line are drawn from a position within the text to a newly added phrase typed legibly in the margin. Presentation of insertions or deletions as part of the original reissue specification is an amendment under 37 CFR 1.173(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims at filing must include status and support
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of the claims made at the time of filing of a reissue application must include a separate paper setting forth the status of all claims (i.e., pending or canceled), and an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent for the changes made to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments at filing must comply with 37 CFR 1.173(b)-(e) and (g); see MPEP § 1453 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charts/tables/chemical formulas not to be split across columns
rubrics_metrics.description: If a chart, table, or chemical formula is amended and it spans two columns of the patent, it should not be split; rather, provide the chart/table/formula in its entirety as part of the column of the patent to which it pertains. The chart/table/formula may extend beyond the width of the column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change in only a part of a word or chemical formula is not permitted; entire words or chemical formulas must be shown as being changed. Deletion of a chemical formula should be shown by brackets which are substantially larger and darker than any in the formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting rules for twice-reissued patents
rubrics_metrics.description: In a second reissue application (reissue of a reissue), double underlining and double bracketing are used in the second reissue application, while bold-faced type and double bracketing appear in the printed patent (the second reissue patent) to indicate further insertions and deletions respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a copy of a first reissue patent is used as the specification of a second reissue application, additions made by the first reissue will already be printed in italics and should remain; applicants need only present additions in the second reissue application as double underlined text; subject matter to be deleted from the first reissue patent should be presented in sets of double brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include certificate of correction or disclaimer changes without markings
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant should include any changes, additions, or deletions that were made by a certificate of correction to the original patent grant in the reissue application without underlining or bracketing. Certificate of correction changes and disclaimer of claim(s) under 37 CFR 1.321(a) should be made without using underlining or brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these are retroactively part of the original patent, they must appear in the printed reissue patent document as part of the original patent (not in italics or bracketed). If improperly submitted with underlining and brackets, the examiner will require correction — possibly requiring a replacement paragraph or a clean copy entered as a substitute specification with a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.183 for waiver of 1.125(d) and 1.173(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibited in reissue applications (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter, i.e., matter not present in the patent sought to be reissued, is excluded from a reissue application in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 251. The claims in the reissue application must be for subject matter which the applicant had the right to claim in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New matter may exist by omission of a feature or step in a method. If new matter has been added anywhere in the application for reissue, form paragraph 14.22.01 may be used. If the new matter is added to the claims or affects the claims, consider also a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph. If new matter is added to the specification and does not affect the claims, consider an objection under 35 U.S.C. 132 using form paragraph 7.28. See MPEP §§ 2161-2163, 2166, and § 608.04(a) for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 14.22.01 for rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251 for new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 251 as being based upon new matter added to the patent for which reissue is sought. The added material which is not supported by the prior patent is as follows: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2, fill in the applicable page and line numbers and provide an explanation of the position as appropriate. Consider also 35 U.S.C. 112(a) rejections if the new matter affects claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original patent requirement — same general invention (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue claims must be for the same invention as that disclosed as being the invention in the original patent. The entire disclosure, not just the claims, is considered in determining what the patentee objectively intended as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law (e.g., In re Amos, Antares Pharma, Forum US v. Flow Valve) establishes that the specification must clearly and unequivocally disclose the newly claimed invention as a separate invention if that is what is sought. Reissue claims may be rejected under § 251 if the original specification does not demonstrate to one skilled in the art that the patentee could have claimed the subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination checklist for original patent requirement (A–C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should review whether (A) the claims presented are described in and enabled by the original patent specification such that 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph is satisfied; (B) nothing in the original patent specification indicates an intent not to claim the subject matter presented in the reissue application; and (C) the newly claimed invention is clearly and unequivocally disclosed in the specification as a separate invention with the claimed combination of features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should discuss any possible rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251 based on failure to meet the original patent requirement with their TQAS or SPRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely file continuing application cannot be corrected by reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a restriction or election of species was made and applicant permitted the elected invention to issue as a patent without filing a continuing application on the non-elected invention(s) or non-claimed distinct subject matter, the non-elected invention(s) and non-claimed distinct subject matter cannot be recovered by filing a reissue application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue applicant’s failure to timely file a continuing application is not considered an error correctable by reissue under 35 U.S.C. 251; reissue claims in such a situation should be rejected under § 251 for lack of any defect in the original patent. Compare with In re Doyle (linking claim) where a linking claim may be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlooked aspects — claims to disclosed but never claimed embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims to separate inventions/embodiments/species that were disclosed but never covered by the claims in the original prosecution are considered 'overlooked aspects' and are not subject to recapture because they were never surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine whether reissue claims are drawn to overlooked aspects, examiner must first determine if the claim meets the original patent requirement. If claims are drawn to overlooked aspects, the examiner should state which claims are drawn to overlooked aspects on the record. See examples and case law (e.g., Youman, Hester, Meyers) for application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture prohibition — cannot reclaim surrendered subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue will not be granted to 'recapture' claimed subject matter which was surrendered in an application to obtain the original patent. Whether a reissue patent violates the rule against recapture of surrendered subject matter in original prosecution is a question of law (see cited case law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims to overlooked aspects are not part of recapture analysis. Examiner must perform recapture analysis when presented with broadened reissue claims and consider definitions and precedent (see MPEP § 1412.02 and cited Federal Circuit cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to recapture analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: Broadening Claim — a reissue claim is 'broadened' where at least one limitation of the patent claims is either completely eliminated or is only presented in a broader way in the reissue claim relative to the broadest patented claim(s). Canceled Claim — a claim canceled from the original application to obtain the patent (including claims replaced by narrower claims). Original Application — includes the prosecution record of the application that issued as the patent and the patent family’s entire prosecution history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions inform whether a reissue claim is a broadened claim and whether recapture applies. Surrender may occur because of prosecution history of related applications; examine family history where relevant (see MBO Laboratories, In re McDonald).
